feasibility_reasoning:
The building blocks exist:
- ga4Mp.server.ts:76-111 is the MP sender and is silent without GA4_API_SECRET (:82-83); :114 is syntheticClientId.
- ga4Client.ts:454 is ga4ClientId.
- track.ts:200 is the client consent gate.
- There is no chunk-graph risk: __root.tsx:77,111 already import ads/consent and ga4Client statically, and track.ts is a lazy chunk (__root.tsx:1063). The listener belongs in track.ts.

The deciding problems are on the server and in dedupe:
- routes/api/public/track.ts:104-160 has no consent, tenant ga4_enabled or signature check. -track.test.ts:3-8 names it an unauthenticated public write path, so "already consent-aware" is false and a relay would turn it into an open GA4 MP proxy.
- visibilitychange:hidden is not terminal. TP-1 resumes on visible, gtag then replays the dataLayer page_view (ga4Client.ts:205-219,433-446), and GA4 does not dedupe page_view.
- session_id from readSession (track.ts:75-93) is not the GA4 session id.
- The target population is narrow, because any interaction or decision already loads gtag (gtagLoadPolicy.ts:59,170-177; ConsentScriptInjector.tsx:36-42).
Full reasoning: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-neweustrategies-dc633fb5/8fd9e8e2-d544-5db4-ae5e-c509c5e3ff6c/scratchpad/phase1/verdicts/third-party--TP-3.md
blocking_issues: Duplicate page_view: visibilitychange:hidden and bfcache pagehide (persisted=true) are not terminal. TP-1 restarts on visible, and gtag.js then replays the queued page_view from window.dataLayer (ga4Client.ts:205-219, 433-446). GA4 dedupes only transaction_id. The design must splice the relayed page_view arguments entry out of dataLayer and set a relayed flag, or send only on the terminal event.

/api/public/track (routes/api/public/track.ts:104-160) has no consent check, no signature and no tenant ga4_enabled read. Consent is enforced only client-side (lib/analytics/track.ts:200). Adding an MP relay that signs with GA4_API_SECRET makes it an open GA4 injection proxy: client_id and page_location can be forged, and the only defence is a per-isolate limiter of 120 burst and 2/s (track.ts:64). It needs a strict schema, one relay per request, a page_location host check against currentTenantHost(), and loadTenantGa4Settings (ga4Mp.server.ts:44), cached.

session_id from readSession() (track.ts:75-93, our nes.analytics.session UUID) is not the GA4 session id, which lives in the _ga_<suffix> cookie. MP also creates no session_start and no attribution, so relayed page_views get (not set) source, medium and landing page. MP derives no geo or device either: the sendGa4ServerEvent body (ga4Mp.server.ts:98-102) lacks timestamp_micros, user_location and device, so the signature needs extending, and forwarding the IP or user-agent is an extra RODO item.

If the bounce event goes through the existing insert path as type page_view, it double-counts first-party page views (semantic/metrics.ts:185; migration 20260912110000:156,184,214). It must be relay-only with no analytics_events insert, or use a non-page_view type.
effect_reasoning:
The code runs only on pagehide or visibilitychange:hidden, and only when hasAnalyticsConsent() is true. Lighthouse ends the trace before navigating away, the headless tab never goes hidden, and the fresh profile has no stored consent (consent.ts:627-630 readLocal() returns null). Each of these alone keeps the code out of the trace.
- Bytes: about 0.3-0.6 KB gzip.
  - In the lazy track chunk: 0 on the critical path.
  - In the root chunk via ga4Client: about 2-3 ms of transfer at 1.6 Mb/s (200 KB/s), under 1 ms of compile at 4x CPU, and no long task.
- TBT, LCP, SI and CLS: 0 on both mobile and desktop.
- The claimed attribution "none (analytics completeness)" is correct.
- The analytics gain is smaller than implied. Gtag already loads on any scroll, pointerdown, touchstart or keydown, or on a consent decision. Visitors without a decision are not consented. So the only population is returning visitors with stored analytics consent who leave with zero interaction before about load+10 s. Without design extensions, their recovered page_views would carry (not set) geo, device and channel.
corrected_estimate:
0 points on mobile and 0 on desktop.
- Byte cost is 0 ms if the listener lives in track.ts, or under 3 ms of non-blocking transfer if it lives in ga4Client.
- Analytics recovery is limited to consented returning zero-interaction bouncers inside the TP-1 window, and those page_views carry degraded attribution.
- Effort is M-to-L once the server hardening is included (schema, host check, tenant settings, dedupe splice, GA4 session-cookie parsing).
better_alternative:
This is an owner decision: give the TP-1 gtag load policy a branch for visitors whose stored decision found at mount grants analytics (hasConsentDecision() && hasAnalyticsConsent(), consent.ts:618-630). For them, keep the v1 timing (load+2 s, 1.5 s quiet, 8 s cap, gtagLoadPolicy.ts:43-47), or load right after load.
- Lighthouse cost is zero, because the PSI fresh profile has no stored consent.
- Gtag keeps its native session, geo, device and attribution.
- It needs no public-endpoint relay, no GA4_API_SECRET exposure and no dedupe logic. Effort S.
- The trade-off is field INP/TBT for returning consented visitors, which ConsentScriptInjector.tsx:36-39 deliberately avoided.
- If an MP relay is still wanted, use it only as a fallback for exits before about load+2 s. Put it in track.ts (lazy), make it relay-only (no insert), splice the page_view out of dataLayer after sending, and read the session id from the _ga_<suffix> cookie.
